subject: Post-call: reduced data horizon request — Medivance
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emma Park <emma@medivance.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — data horizon constraints and next steps

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap so we have a shared record and clear next steps.

Summary of what we heard from Medivance:
- Primary requirement: PII/PHI must not be persisted beyond request completion — preference for 0-retention for any sensitive fields.
- Non-PII conversational logs can be kept for a short troubleshooting window; suggested target by your team is 7 days maximum.
- KV cache: you want the option to disable model-side KV persistence for sessions that touch PHI.
- Data residency: traffic will route from US regions; no EU residency required for this initial pilot.
- Procurement note: you will need a formal exception/statement for our standard 90-day operational logs to share with your security/compliance team.

What Redwood can offer (high level):
- Ephemeral mode for inputs tagged as PHI: model inputs are processed in-memory, KV cache eviction immediate, no disk-backed log retention.
- Short-term logs: configurable retention windows (we can set to 7 days for non-PII by policy).
- Optional dedicated/private deployment if you prefer tenant isolation and KMS control.
- Evidence we can provide: SOC 2 report summary, architecture diagram for ephemeral processing, and a sample minimal-retention config for your infra/security review.

Attachments: I attached an initial proposal (redwood-data-horizon-proposal.pdf) and a quick Q&A (medivance-minimal-retention-qna.pdf) that answers the technical carveouts we discussed.

Requested next steps (proposed):
1) Emma: confirm whether Medivance requires 0-retention for all message metadata or only for fields you classify as PHI.
2) We will produce: a one-page exception letter + minimal-retention config and an architecture sketch by EOD 8/19.
3) If procurement wants, we can kick off a pilot SOW (2–4 weeks) scoped to evaluate ephemeral mode on a small user cohort — Redwood can provide a pilot addendum.

If that matches your understanding, I’ll route the exception letter and config to you and laura will join next week for a short tech sync.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

-----
Attachment stubs:
- redwood-data-horizon-proposal.pdf (proposal, 4 pages)
- medivance-minimal-retention-qna.pdf (Q&A, 2 pages)
From: Emma Park <emma@medivance.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medivance.com
Date: 2026-08-19T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — data horizon constraints and next steps

Thanks Jordan — helpful recap. A few clarifying questions before we share with security/procurement:

1) When you say "ephemeral mode" for PHI, does Redwood also avoid writing any request/response metadata to logs (request IDs, timestamps)? We need assurances that anything tying a user identifier to a prompt is not retained.
2) Is there an option to fully disable KV caching at the model layer per-session (not just expire on a schedule)?
3) We will likely need an official exception letter from Redwood (signed) that specifies the exact retention windows and controls we will rely on for our audit.

Procurement asked if you can also provide a sample SOW for a 14-day pilot (we want to evaluate both behavior and telemetry collection limits). Please include clear acceptance criteria for both privacy and performance.

Emma Park
Head of Product Security
Medivance

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-19T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — data horizon constraints and next steps

Jordan / Aditya — quick internal note before we respond to Emma:

- Answer to Q1: We can produce an exception letter that explicitly states that any fields labeled as PHI will not be written to persistent logs; system-level telemetry (aggregated metrics) will be retained but will be de-identified at ingestion. We should avoid claiming "no metadata at all" — better to specify what we keep (aggregated, non-identifying counts, error traces without user identifiers).
- Answer to Q2: Yes, per-session KV caching can be disabled. We need to confirm downstream latency impact with the runtime team, but we can present two pilot modes: (A) KV disabled for PHI sessions (recommended for strict privacy) or (B) KV enabled but evicted immediately after request completion.
- Pilot SOW: propose 14-day pilot with two cohorts: cohort A (ephemeral mode, KV disabled) and cohort B (short-retain mode, 7 days). Acceptance criteria: no PHI persisted in logs (verified by us with a test script), latency within 20% of baseline, and telemetry availability for error triage.

I can draft the exception letter and pilot SOW. Jordan — can you confirm which deployment we should propose (Hosted with ephemeral controls vs Redwood Private)? My preference: offer Hosted ephemeral first (faster), and mention Private as an option if Medivance insists on tenant isolation/KMS.

Laura
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, procurement@medivance.com
Date: 2026-08-20T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — reduced data horizon request — Medivance

Emma — thanks for the questions, and apologies for the slow follow-up. Attached is the one-page exception letter and the updated proposal we discussed. Key commitments in the letter:

- PHI/PII fields: 0-retention. Any data flagged by your integration as "sensitive" will be processed in-memory and not written to persistent logs or disk-backed caches.
- Metadata: request IDs and timestamps used for debugging will not be linked to user identifiers in persisted storage; aggregated telemetry (de-identified counts and error buckets) will be retained for 30 days for operational monitoring.
- KV cache: per-session KV can be fully disabled. We will ship a per-session flag for the pilot.
- Pilot offer: 14-day pilot with two cohorts (ephemeral vs 7-day short retention). Redwood will provide the test harness that verifies no PHI written to logs.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether "0-retention" must apply to metadata (IDs/timestamps) or only to payload/PII — that will determine how we phrase the exception letter.
2) If Medivance agrees, I’ll route a 14-day pilot SOW + DocuSign link to procurement.
3) Technical sync: propose 30 minutes next week — laura, aditya and I will join to walk the pilot config.
